items.title: Record supply growth pushes container fleet towards 50m teu by 2030
points: The global containership fleet is heading towards an unprecedented 50m teu by 2030, setting the stage for a potentially devastating oversupply crisis and enormous downward pressure on freight rates.

New analysis from Sea-Intelligence shows the fleet expanding from today’s 34m teu to 40m teu by the second quarter of 2028 and 50m teu by the third quarter of 2030, the largest capacity expansion in container shipping history.
Combined with an estimated 8% effective capacity boost from the return of Asia-Europe services to the Suez Canal, cumulative supply growth could exceed 50% by the end of the decade.
The consultancy calculates that quarterly newbuilding deliveries will average 1m teu between 2027 and 2030, peaking at an extraordinary 1.8m teu in the third quarter of 2028.
Even if carriers repeated the record demolition levels of 2016 every year through 2030, this would absorb less than 17% of incoming capacity, leaving annual fleet growth averaging 8.5%.

items.title: ‘Delhi AQI crossed 3,000’: AAP's Saurabh Bharadwaj alleges ‘AQI data fraud’ by government

In a video shared on X, Bharadwaj claimed that the government had installed 20 new monitoring stations in open areas surrounded by greenery and was sprinkling water around stations in heavily polluted localities to lower their readings.
Nearly 80% of the functioning stations reported ‘severe’ air quality between 10 pm on Diwali and 6 am the following morning.
At 9 pm on Diwali night, the last available reading before the number of reporting stations dropped sharply, 61% of the 57 stations reporting data had recorded an AQI of 400 or above.
An HT analysis of CPCB data found that 13 newly installed AQI monitoring stations on the city's periphery may be affecting Delhi's overall pollution readings.

items.title: On Diwali night, Delhi's PM2.5 readings climbed towards 1,000, then went blank

items.title: Congress slams Modi govt. for being in ‘denial’ on impact of air pollution on mortality
points: Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh cited the FICCI-EY report and pointed out that it categorically states that around 2 million deaths (about 22% of total) were attributable to air pollution in India in 2023.
The Modi government has long been in denial on the impact of air pollution on mortality in the country, the former Environment Minister said.
It has rejected, both in Parliament and outside, a number of studies on the grounds that they are not India-specific and that the impacts are not direct and uniquely attributable, Ramesh said on X.

As per the notice, the changes have been introduced in XAT exam pattern, seats, B-School opportunities and XAT 2025 to 2026 question papers and answer keys.
According to the new changes, candidates can get XAT 2025 and XAT 2026 question papers with answer key by completing their XAT 2027 application process by November 11, 2026.
The last date to apply for the exam is December 6, 2026.
This year, more seats have been introduced at XLRI Jamshedpur, PGDM-HRM seat intake increased from 180 to 240.
The XAT exam is set to be conducted on January 3, 2027 for three hours from 2 pm to 5 pm and the admit card for the same will be released on December 20, 2026.
The exam comprises four sections such as, Verbal Ability and Logical Reasoning (VALR), Decision Making (DM), Quantitative Aptitude & Data Interpretation (QA & DI) and General knowledge (GK).

points: The Kozhikode City police have arrested a 34-year-old man in connection with an ongoing investigation into a series of incidents involving extortion, criminal intimidation and impersonation.
Nishad, was arrested from Kondotty in Malappuram district on Sunday evening.
According to the First Information Report (FIR) registered at the Medical College police station here, the accused has been charged under Sections 308(2) and 204 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
The police said he was a habitual offender, with multiple cases registered against him under the jurisdictions of the Kondotty and Manjeri police stations.

His criminal history includes cases registered at the Kondotty police station under Sections 21(b) and 29(1) of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, Section 151 of the CrPC, Section 27(b) of the NDPS Act, and Section 170 of the BNS.

items.title: Motherhood should not come at cost of women's careers: NCW chief
points: New Delhi, NCW Chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar has said motherhood should not come at the cost of a woman's career, stressing the need for shared parenting and stronger institutional support to help women remain in the workforce after childbirth.

In an interview with PTI, the National Commission for Women chief said raising a child is the equal responsibility of both parents and called for a supportive environment to enable women to balance their professional aspirations with motherhood.
"When a child comes into the home, the responsibility of that child belongs to everyone.
It lies with the mother as well as the father.
It is the equal responsibility of both," she said.
Women should be able to pursue their careers, fulfil their dreams and achieve their aspirations without having to compromise on motherhood, she added.
They will continue their careers," the NCW chief said.

points: The drug menace in Punjab is no longer just a political talking point; it is increasingly becoming a test of the Bhagwant Mann government's credibility, the effectiveness of its policing machinery and the ability of opposition parties to offer an…

On Saturday, when Punjab Agriculture Minister Gurmeet Singh Khuddian visited Lallbai village in Muktsar district, a woman confronted him over the alleged open sale of drugs in neighbouring villages.
A day earlier, a 27-year-old member of a village anti-drug committee, Amandeep Singh, was shot at by armed assailants at his residence in Kaleke village of Barnala district.
The Barnala firing assumes greater significance as it comes less than a month after anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota was shot dead in Mansa on October 13.

items.title: Devotees throng Tawang Monastery to pay respects to sacred relics of Shakyamuni Buddha
points: Over 31,000 devotees and visitors thronged the Tawang Monastery in Arunachal Pradesh over seven days to pay their respects to the sacred relics of Shakyamuni Buddha, as an exposition concluded on Saturday, marking the end of its first leg in the Himalayan…
The sacred relics arrived in Tawang on October 31 from the National Museum in New Delhi before being transported to Bomdila by the Indian Air Force on November 8 for the next phase of the exposition.
They will remain open for public darshan at TGL Monastery (Lower Gompa) until November 13.
After Bomdila, the sacred relics will be taken to the Golden Pagoda in Namsai, where devotees can seek blessings from November 14 to 20.
They are scheduled to be taken back to the National Museum on November 21.
Chief minister Pema Khandu ceremonially received the relics on their arrival in Tawang in the presence of Union culture and tourism minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat.

6 Of Family Killed After Fire At Goldsmith's House In Madhya Pradesh's Seoni
points: Six members of a family were killed, and four others suffered injuries after a massive fire broke out at the three-storey house of a goldsmith in Madhya Pradesh's Seoni district early on Monday, police said.
The incident occurred between 4 am and 4.30 am, a day after Diwali, at the house of goldsmith Kundan Lal Soni near a Jain temple in Mahavir Ward in Chhapara town, they said.
Ten persons were present in the house at the time of the incident.
Six of them died, and four were evacuated, Sub-Divisional Officer of Police Apoorva Bhalavi, who was present at the spot, told PTI over the phone.
The fire brigade and rescue teams later brought the fire under control, he said.
Those who died have been identified as Kundan Lal Soni (75), his wife Rajkumari Soni (65), Ritu Soni (42), Smriti Soni (40), Surya Soni (45) and Aditya Soni (16), he added.

points: A man in Chhattisgarh allegedly murdered his cousin's four-year-old son and removed his kidneys, lungs and eyes in a bid to sell the organs online after searching social media for ways to earn quick money, police said.

The 27-year-old accused, identified as Basudev, alias Tangnu, was arrested on Sunday after the child's body was found stuffed in a sack and dumped in a pit at a field in Lodhenapath Mahua village of Jashpur district, they said.

items.title: TN sets up TNICC to drive mega infra, revenue generating projects
points: Chennai, The Tamil Nadu government has established TNICC, as a wholly-owned state PSU to give a significant push to rapid urbanisation and large-scale public development.

The newly formed corporate body aims to execute major state government infrastructure projects valued above ₹200 crore while driving revenue generation through unused government lands and competitive private-sector tenders, according to a GO issued on Monday.
The initiative stems from a recent announcement made on the floor of the Assembly by the Minister for Public Works and Sports Development.

Driven by the state's expanding infrastructure demands, the Tamil Nadu Infrastructure and Construction Corporation is designed as an agile, self-sustaining institutional mechanism equipped with professional expertise and operational flexibility.

Operating as a Project Management Consultant , the corporation will centralise project management, implement modern technologies, and provide high-quality architectural designs and quality control services.

Its operational scope encompasses developing modern townships, industrial hubs, technology parks, IT cities, and business parks, alongside optimising underutilised government land parcels to create sustainable state revenue.

items.title: Six burnt alive as speeding car crashes into pole, divider in UP’s Muzaffarnagar
points: Six people were burnt alive after a speeding car crashed into an electric pole and divider before catching fire on a national highway in the Muzaffarnagar district of Uttar Pradesh early on Monday, officials aware of the matter said.

Additional SP (Rural) Akshay Sanjay Mahadik said police received information about the accident, which occurred on the Panipat-Khatima National Highway around 25km from the Muzaffarnagar district headquarters at 4.50am.
“Six people travelling in the car were burnt.
They were immediately shifted to hospital by the Titawi police.
Efforts are underway to establish their identities.
The law and order situation at the spot is normal,” Mahadik said.
The victims, believed to be residents of Haryana’s Jind district, were travelling towards Haridwar when the accident occurred, people aware of the matter said.
The vehicle first rammed into an electricity pole before smashing through nearly 10 metres of the divider and overturning onto the opposite carriageway.

items.title: Indian-Americans Ranjeev Puri, Priya Sundareshan elected to head Michigan, Arizona legislatures
points: State Representative Ranjeev Puri was elected Speaker of Michigan’s House of Representatives after the US midterm elections last week.
State Senator Priya Sundareshan was chosen to lead Arizona’s Senate as its President.
Born in 1984 to Sikh immigrants from Punjab, Puri started his political career by working on President Barack Obama’s presidential campaigns in 2008 and 2012.
Puri was elected to the Michigan House in 2020 and soon took over as majority whip, responsible for securing votes and ensuring party discipline in 2023-24.

Speaking in a television interview after his election, Puri attributed the Democratic Party’s victory to widespread dissatisfaction with the Iran war and the impact of US President Trump’s tariffs that decimated the state’s agricultural sector.
She took over as her party’s leader in the Arizona Senate in January 2025.

He said Sundareshan will fight for public schools, Arizona’s water, and democracy, and to protect their communities and all Arizonans at a time of rising hate targeting Indian and South Asian Americans.

items.title: Andhra local body elections: TDP-led coalition wins two-third of zilla parishad seats
points: Andhra Pradesh’s ruling alliance, led by the Telugu Desam Party, won two-thirds of the Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency (ZPTC) and Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituency (MPTC) seats, the state election commission (SEC) announced Sunday night.

According to SEC, the TDP won 406 of the 582 ZPTC seats for which elections were held, while its alliance partners, Jana Sena Party (JSP) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), secured 73 and 20 seats, respectively.
The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) finished second with 76 seats, marginally ahead of Jana Sena in the district-level governing council elections.
The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), Congress, and Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) won no ZPTC seats.
The TDP posted strong performances in Nellore district, winning 26 of the 30 ZPTC seats.
It also won 22 of 30 seats in Srikakulam, 22 of 28 in Anantapur, 21 of 32 in Sri Sathya Sai, 21 of 31 in Tirupati, and 21 of 25 in Prakasam.

Banks step up pressure on Havila Shipping over $78m debt dispute
points: Norwegian offshore vessel owner Havila Shipping is facing renewed enforcement action from three major banks seeking to establish security liens over the company’s assets in connection with a long-running debt restructuring dispute.
DNB, Swedbank, and Danske Bank have submitted a new request for attachment liens covering NOK779m ($78m), comprising NOK713m in principal and approximately NOK65m in accrued interest.
The latest move follows a ruling by Norway’s Borgarting Court of Appeal on October 19, which went against Havila in its dispute with the lenders over a restructuring agreement dating back to 2020.
Havila has said it disagrees with the judgment and intends to appeal to the Norwegian Supreme Court.
The deadline for filing the appeal is November 19.
The dispute centres on whether Havila breached the restructuring agreement by refinancing debt owed to lenders that had opted for a cash settlement in December 2024.

items.title: Meyer Werft sets up offshore business to handle $2.8bn converter orderbook
points: German shipbuilding group Meyer Werft is setting up a dedicated offshore business to manage its growing involvement in North Sea converter platform construction.

The new company, Neptun Offshore, will bring together the group’s offshore converter activities and hold its 50% stake in Neptun Smulders Offshore Renewables (NSORe), a joint venture with Belgian steel construction specialist Smulders.
NSORe secured two major offshore converter contracts from German transmission system operator 50Hertz earlier this year for the LanWin3 and LanWin6 grid connection projects in the North Sea.

The joint venture’s share of the contracts is valued at approximately €2.5bn ($2.8bn), with a substantial proportion of the work expected to take place in the German state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, including at Neptun Werft’s facilities in Rostock.
Both projects involve 2GW offshore converter platforms designed to transmit electricity generated by North Sea wind farms to the German power grid.
Neptun Offshore will be a wholly owned subsidiary of Meyer Werft, headed by Malte Poelmann, who already serves as managing director of NSORe alongside Dieter Weyns.

items.title: ADES bags $117m ONGC drilling contracts for jackup duo
points: Saudi offshore drilling contractor ADES has secured two three-year contracts from India’s Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) worth a combined SAR439.6m ($117.2m).
The awards cover the standard jackup rigs Key Singapore and Admarine 10, with each unit securing a firm three-year drilling assignment in Indian waters.
ADES said the contract value includes mobilisation fees and covers the firm periods of both rigs.

The two units are expected to complete their existing drilling campaigns by the end of 2026 before moving into the new ONGC assignments, which are scheduled to begin by the end of the first quarter of 2027.
ADES has been expanding its international offshore drilling business through long-term contracting arrangements with national oil companies and maintains a substantial presence in the Indian market.
The latest awards add six combined rig-years of firm work to the contractor’s portfolio.

items.title: ADNOC Drilling chosen for $315m Kuwait offshore rig deals

Kuwait Oil Company awarded the two contracts to the Abu Dhabi-listed drilling contractor after ADNOC Drilling submitted the lowest compliant bids, meeting the technical specifications and other requirements.
The maximum combined contract cost is approximately $315m, although the individual contract values, rig identities, durations, and expected commencement dates have not been disclosed.
The approval comes as Kuwait moves to expand offshore exploration and development following a series of discoveries in its territorial waters.
Kuwait Oil Company has recently made discoveries at Nokhatha, Julaia, and Jazza, adding to its oil and gas potential.
The company has been preparing further offshore drilling and seismic programmes to build on those discoveries.
